question: What comes back of a programme whose every number is known, when it goes through Dolby's encoders and `oadec` reads the stream: across the frame rate a master names, its bed, the number of its objects, how they move, what is said of them besides a place, whether the elements sound together or one after another, and what the encoder is told to make of it? Do the tools take what `oadec` writes in every one of those, is every stream they make of it clean, do the two decoders make the same elements of every stream, and what does a second encode of a decode keep?
method: A row is one value of each of seven axes; 51 rows are a pairwise design, every value of every axis with every value of every other in some row, of 40 320 combinations (`tools/interop.py plan`). The scene of a row gives every object and every channel of the bed a tone of its own, 60 Hz for the LFE, 150 to 550 Hz for the bed and 600 Hz to 3,2 kHz for the objects, none nearer another than 50 Hz and all below the lowest frequency a core can begin to couple its channels at, so that an element is known by its sound whatever the encoder numbers it. The first three objects move as the row says, the first says what the row says besides its place, and the elements sound together through nine seconds or in turn, each alone for 0,75 s at every place it rests at. `oadec atmos-author` writes the master. Each row goes five ways: to E-AC-3 JOC (`dee_ddpjoc_encoder` of the Dolby Media Encoder, at the rate of the row); through Dolby's Conversion Tool to ADM BWF and then to that encoder; as a second generation, the first stream decoded by `oadec decode` with its defaults to a master and to ADM BWF (`--dolby-origin-tag`) and encoded again; and to TrueHD (`dee_dthd_encoder`, the encoder axis picking 12, 14 or 16 elements). The seven rows whose master names the Lo/Ro warp mode make their second generations once more with `--warp-mode stream`. Of every stream: what `info`, `oamd`, `emdf` and `verify` say; `oadec decode --format damf --no-bed-conform`; for the E-AC-3 ones the object decode of the Dolby Reference Player (`dlbac3dec out-ch-config=21`), lined up by where the programme begins and held to oadec's sample by sample, element by element; and the decode held to the scene: for every stretch an object rests at a place (a rest), the power of its tone in every element, the element that has most of it (the carrier) and its share, where the carrier says it is against where the scene put it (the largest difference in a coordinate; "at the place" is within 0,05), and when the carrier first says a place the object was told to move to. Beside the matrix, 33 probes: one object alone over a silent LFE with one thing said of it, through both encoders. Dolby's tools are run as they stand and only what they write is read.
commands: python tools/interop.py probe --work <dir>/probes; python tools/interop.py probe --path truehd --work <dir>/probes-truehd

reading: Dolby's encoders and Conversion Tool take what `oadec` writes in every row of the design, every stream they make of it is clean, and the two decoders make the same elements of every E-AC-3 one at lag 0. What sounds alone comes back whole: in one element, at its place and at its level, with every move made, whatever the frame rate, the bed, the number of objects and the rate. What sounds together is the encoder's to code: at its place where the scene is no larger than the stream, in clusters where it is larger, and in JOC with a part of a tone in other elements. Nothing a master says of an object besides its place is in a stream: the encoders render a lock, a zone and a size and drop a gain, so a decode has none of them to give back. The bed of a stream is the LFE and the other channels of a master's bed are objects at their speakers' places. The Conversion Tool's ADM and the master encode to the same bytes, and so do this decoder's master and its ADM of a stream; a second generation keeps what the first kept where the elements sound in turn, and loses the warp mode unless the decode names it. The TrueHD encoder's streams of one master are not the same bytes from run to run and decode to the same samples, so two TrueHD encodes that differ say nothing of what was changed without two encodes of nothing changed. Not asked here: trims, which the scenes cannot say; more than twenty objects; material that is not tones; and 96 kHz, which the encoders refuse.
